scope: Independent pre-implementation review of the contract, inactive model and runtime plan; no production changes.

input_verification.root_recomputed_from: SHA256 of canonical compact sorted-key files array

findings.title: The proxy runtime cannot import the required observer client
evidence: /usr/bin/python3 is Python 3.12.3 and import psycopg fails with ModuleNotFoundError in the reviewed environment
contract.json control_transport.observer and observer_details.peer_gate require an in-process psycopg observer through canonical connect
findings.impact: The specified observer and readiness path cannot run with the current bootstrap interpreter. The contract identifies new module hashes but does not specify a dependency-provisioned proxy interpreter, its identity, or bootstrap changes needed to use it.
findings.required_change: Specify and bind a supported proxy Python interpreter and psycopg/libpq dependency installation and version identity, update bootstrap and daemon loaded-identity verification accordingly, and require clean bootstrap plus observer lifecycle tests under that exact interpreter. Preserve ordinary bootstrap before the lazy observer, including on a fresh cluster before the role and configured database exist.

findings.title: Atomic replacement does not serialize shared journal updates
evidence: contract.json journal_details defines one file with separate context and observer entries and atomic replace/fsync
control_transport.observer uses an owned thread while the proxy runs concurrent lifecycle, admission and cleanup operations
contract does not prescribe serialization or transactional merge for full-state updates
findings.impact: Two overlapping read-modify-write operations can each atomically replace the file with a stale snapshot, losing the other durable RESERVED, CONNECTING, KEYED or BOUND entry. After a crash, recovery may wrongly see an empty reservation and admit a replacement while the prior backend remains owned. Atomic rename guarantees individual file integrity, not preservation of concurrent updates.
findings.required_change: Specify a single serialized journal authority or equivalent cross-thread synchronization and linearization of each full-state update; no backend-open attempt or authority exposure may occur before its exact mutation is durable. Require concurrent observer/context update interleavings, crash barriers and restart tests proving neither entry can be lost.

assessment: The current bootstrap starts the ordinary proxy and executes role/database creation before the proposed lazy observer; the contract explicitly preserves that ordering, but executable clean-cluster verification is still required.

Pre-key context and observer uncertainty and PostgreSQL exhaustion from ordinary disconnected backend tails are explicitly fail-closed availability limitations; they are not treated as blockers to this safety-oriented contract.
Protocol execution fencing, exact identity observation and secret-bound cancellation are stipulated, but the model does not prove their implementation correspondence.
Full-quota history processing within the fixed deadline and the target 4-vCPU/8-GiB deployment remain measured acceptance obligations, not established performance or commercial readiness.
limitations: No production implementation or runtime acceptance was executed.
The 28 claims and 33 plan entries were counted and reviewed as finite design obligations; this review does not assert independent Lean builds or runtime proofs.
Pre-key UNKNOWN may persist, and ordinary backend tails can exhaust PostgreSQL slots; neither prompt recovery nor guaranteed availability is claimed.
All six exact-root approvals and two isolated matching clean model builds remain activation prerequisites.
